description: The cross-language crypto vectors that pin device<->server parity. Each is reproduced byte-for-byte by independent Go and Rust implementations and is asserted in CI, so a value here is ground truth, not illustration. These are the anchors that let the server trust a proof minted on a device it never shares a secret with.

request_proof_hmac.purpose: Per-request proof: the device HMACs a domain-separated preimage with its per-install key; the server reconstructs the same preimage and key-derivation and recomputes the tag. Equal tag => the request came from a sealed, attested install.
request_proof_hmac.reproduce: HMAC-SHA256(key="kseal-test-instance-key", preimage) where preimage = len-prefixed(domain, token_id, request_hash, nonce) || int64_be(sequence)

kill_switch_ed25519.purpose: Remote disable/enable for a (tenant, app, build) scope, verified offline by the device against a pinned signing key. A forged or altered command is a no-op (fail-safe).
kill_switch_ed25519.preimage_layout: u32_be(len)||DOMAIN || u32_be(len)||tenant_id || u32_be(len)||app_id || u32_be(len)||build_hash || u64_be(command) || u64_be(version) || u64_be(issued_at) || u32_be(len)||reason

signed_config_ed25519.purpose: Authenticate a whole policy envelope (config bytes + version + ttl + key_id) so the device can verify policy offline behind a CDN and reject rollbacks/staleness.

demo_hashes.note: Reproducible identifiers used across every fixture and doc. Each is a plain sha256 of the listed input string so any reader can regenerate it.
